goldens.comment: After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.
goldens.reasoning: C1 points out that the federated model is built with createFromValues and has no id, so removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator will not remove it. That is the same issue as the null id in G2.

candidates: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:80 - Used-up federated recovery codes are removed through the local store API, which does nothing for them.. `getCredential` can now return a credential from user storage. If all of its codes are used, the code still calls `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`, which only deletes from the local database. The federated model may have no id at all: the test provider builds it with `createFromValues` and no id. The user-storage copy is never removed, so the user keeps a credential with no codes left and is not sent to the setup required action that normally follows. Fix: when the credential is federated, remove it through the user storage path, for example `disableCredentialType` or `updateCredential`.

testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:326 - Federated recovery codes are never used up and any code is accepted.. `isValid` returns true if the input matches any stored code. It never removes the matched code. The local `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider` consumes each code on use, but nothing does that for a federated credential. `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` then rebuilds the model from all stored codes, so the login page always asks for the first code while any of the 12 is accepted, and a code can be used again forever. This is the reference provider for the new path, so the test cannot catch the broken one-time-use rule. Fix: check only the requested next code, then remove it and persist the remaining list (for example through `updateCredential`), or have the authenticator update the federated credential after a successful login.
